stem: During a traffic spike planning session, an e-commerce team explains two needs: capacity must already be in place for a specific calendar date they know in advance, and separately, an unplanned spike should trigger a larger capacity jump the more severely a CloudWatch alarm is breached. Which TWO Auto Scaling policies together meet these needs? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Target tracking that holds one metric at a constant value
Scheduled scaling that changes capacity at a set date and time
Predictive scaling that forecasts capacity from historical recurring load
A scheduled scaling action already configured for last year's peak sales date
Step scaling that sizes each capacity change to the alarm's breach amount

rationale: Scheduled scaling that changes capacity at a set date and time matches the known-calendar-date requirement. Step scaling that sizes each capacity change to the alarm's breach amount matches the requirement for a larger jump on a more severe unplanned spike. Target tracking only holds one metric at one constant value; it does not give a differently sized reaction to different breach severities. Predictive scaling forecasts from a recurring historical pattern, not from a single known calendar date the team already has in hand. A scheduled scaling action already configured for last year's peak sales date is the same feature correctly used, but for the wrong date: it is scheduled scaling, just not pointed at the date this team needs capacity in place for.
